The test image shows a tomato leaf with a prominent white/gray powdery or fuzzy coating covering most of the leaf surface. Leaf veins are visible through the coating. The leaf appears somewhat curled. Top candidates: **Powdery Mildew**, **Leaf Mold**, **Gray Mold**.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Now I need to cover the remaining classes. Let me view one from each of the unviewed classes.

I've now used all 16 reference image views. Let me make my analysis.

**Test image analysis:**
- Tomato leaf showing extensive white/gray powdery/dusty coating covering most of the leaf surface
- Leaf veins visible through the coating
- Coating is fine-grained and mealy in texture (characteristic of fungal sporulation)
- Leaf appears slightly curled

**Reference comparison:**
- **Powdery Mildew (CDDM_1036.jpg)**: Shows tomato leaves covered with white powdery growth — very close match to the test image in terms of the dusty white coating pattern and extent
- **Powdery Mildew (CDDM_1061.jpg)**: Light gray/white powdery coating on a leaf — matches texture
- **Leaf Mold references**: Show yellowing patches and olive discoloration, not the white powdery coating seen in test image — not a match
- **Gray Mold**: Showed fruit rot and microscopy, not leaf powdery coating — not a match
- All other classes (Early Blight, Septoria, Anthracnose, Bacterial Speck, CMV, TSWV): Show discrete spots, lesions, mosaic patterns, or fruit damage — clearly not matching the diffuse white powdery coating

The white mealy coating covering the leaf is the hallmark sign of Powdery Mildew infection.
